title: The 5th Corps Breaks Out: Dudakovic's Gamble at Bihac
content:
By autumn 1994, the Bihac pocket remained isolated from the rest of government-held territory. ARBiH 5th Corps, commanded by General Atif Dudakovic and headquartered at Bihac, faced VRS forces around the eastern and southern perimeter, APWB forces under Fikret Abdic around Velika Kladusa, and the Republic of Serbian Krajina across the Croatian border. BB2 pp. 536-538 preserve the APWB order of battle, the ARBiH 5th Corps order of battle, and the source trail for fighting around Bihac in 1994.

In October 1994, the 5th Corps launched Operation Grmec from the Bihac pocket toward VRS positions south and east of Bihac. The named operational geography in this packet is deliberately narrow: Bihac, the Grabez and Grmec approaches, and the route toward Bosanska Krupa. The immediate operational result was an ARBiH gain outside the pocket, not a decisive change in the wider western Bosnia front.

The advance forced a VRS response. Later in 1994, VRS forces, units from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and APWB remnants counterattacked and pushed the 5th Corps back toward Bihac. The breakout therefore belongs in the Codex as a bounded operational episode: a 5th Corps attack from an isolated pocket, a short-lived gain on the Grabez/Grmec approaches, and a subsequent counteroffensive that restored the crisis around the enclave.
